newsitem.title: USA: New Clinton team includes Richardson, Daley, Reno.
newsitem.headline: New Clinton team includes Richardson, Daley, Reno.

text.p: President Bill Clinton was to announce a string of Cabinet nominations on Friday, including Representative Bill Richardson as U.N. ambassador and political ally William Daley as commerce secretary, officials said.
They said Clinton also planned to announce that Attorney General Janet Reno would remain the nation's top law enforcement official and Robert Rubin would continue as Treasury Secretary.
The president planned to make the announcement at an afternoon news conference in a government office building adjacent to the White House.
Rubin's reappointment was not in doubt but Reno's had been subject to some speculation because of some past frictions with White House insiders.

Richardson, a 49-year-old New Mexico Democrat of Hispanic descent who is close to Clinton personally, has been involved in several high-profile rescues of U.S. citizens detained in foreign countries and other delicate diplomatic assignments.

Daley, a lawyer, banker and brother of Chicago Mayor Richard Daley, is a veteran Clinton backer and trouble-shooter. He spearheaded the White House drive for congressional approval of the North American Free Trade Agreement in 1993, and more recently helped organise and orchestrate the Chicago Democratic Convention in August.
Richardson would replace Madeleine Albright, whom Clinton nominated last week to be the first woman Secretary of State.
Daley would succeed Clinton confidant Mickey Kantor, who plans to return to private life.

Clinton's decision to retain Reno ended weeks of speculation about her future. White House officials were bothered by her independent streak and her alacrity in asking for independent counsels to probe alleged administration misdeeds. Clinton was known to share their reservations.
But officials said the president had a good meeting with the 56-year-old former Florida prosecutor on Thursday night and asked her to stay in his second-term lineup.
The sources said Clinton also planned to name several other key members of his second-term team on Friday.

They said he had selected economic policy aide Gene Sperling, 38, to head the National Economic Council, which coordinates U.S. economic policy much as the National Security Council coordinates defence and foreign policy.
He was also expected to nominate Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky to permanent status.
All this would still leave a number of other vacancies to be filled, including the top jobs at the Departments of Labour, Transportation, Energy and Housing.

Another key job is the chairman of the president's Council of Economic Advisers, but White House officials said Clinton had not yet settled on a candidate for it. Joseph Stiglitz, who now holds the post, has announced he is leaving to become chief economist of the World Bank.

Alan Blinder, a former CEA member and vice chairman of the Federal Reserve Board, has been sounded out about returning to the White House to head the council, but has told friends he is be reluctant to do so.
Blinder left his job at the Federal Reserve in January to teach at Princeton University.
